# Research question

**Research question:**

Among adults aged 60 to 75 in primary care diagnosed with COPD, is the number of **COPD exacerbations** that require treatment during the previous 12 months associated with how far they are able walk within 6 minutes measured at baseline and six times more over 6 months, taking into account their usual **level of physical activity**?

> It would be beneficial to understand whether there is a pattern in how far the participants are able to walk within 6 minutes during each follow up with how many **COPD exacerbations** they had that required treatment in the previous 12 months and whether their usual **level of physical activity** also affected the distance they are able to walk. If there is, then a further investigation into how much it affects and whether a baseline for each permutation exists by finding their means and standard deviation (or median and IQR). It is worth knowing the relationships between these variables as it could serve as a promoting point for having a better physical activity level despite having COPD.

Similar question but instead of **COPD exacerbations**, **smoking status** instead.



# Data import and structure
```{r import}
# Baseline data
baseline = read.table('data/Baseline_Data.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t')
str(baseline)
summary(baseline)

# Visits data
visits = read.table('data/Visits_Data.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t')
str(visits)
summary(visits)
visits_per_id = aggregate(visit ~ ID, data = visits, FUN = length)
unique(visits_per_id$visit)
nrow(visits_per_id[visits_per_id$visit == 7, ])
nrow(visits_per_id[visits_per_id$visit == 6, ])
```
The baseline data contains 501 rows of data with 10 columns (variables). Some of the data types from the baseline data are not automatically the correct data type according to the dictionary and also contain some NA values. Possible duplicate ID shown from the baseline summary with 501 observations but only 500 unique values. The visits data contains 3466 rows of data with 3 columns (variables), each participants are expected to have 7 visits total but 20 participants only have 6 visits while 478 participants have the full 7 visits.


# Data quality assessment and cleaning
## Baseline data
```{r clean-baseline}
# Duplicates
baseline[duplicated(baseline$ID), 'ID']
baseline[baseline$ID == 'COPD000078', ] # Exact same row, index 78 and 501

# Factor columns: sex, smoker, phy_activity, diabetes, ethnicity, inhaler
# Sex
unique(baseline$sex)
baseline[baseline$sex == 12, ] # 1 row

# Smoker
unique(baseline$smoker)
baseline[baseline$smoker == -999, ] # 3 rows

# phy_activity
unique(baseline$phy_activity)
baseline[baseline$phy_activity == 'Hihg' &
    !is.na(baseline$phy_activity), ] # 6 rows; Typo 'Hihg'

# Diabetes
unique(baseline$diabetes) # No issues

# Ethnicity
unique(baseline$ethnicity)
baseline[baseline$ethnicity == 4 &
    !is.na(baseline$ethnicity), -1] # 4 rows; Unclear error

# Inhaler
unique(baseline$inhaler) # No issues

# Numerical / continuous columns: age, bmi
numerical_baseline_cols = c('age', 'bmi')
summary(baseline[, numerical_baseline_cols])

# BMI
head(baseline[order(baseline$bmi, decreasing = TRUE),
    c('ID', 'bmi')]) # Irregular BMI values of 288.0, 295.0

# Exacerbations
unique(baseline$exacerbations) # No issues

# Handling data issues
baseline = baseline[-501, ] # Duplicate
baseline$sex[baseline$sex == 12] = NA  # Sex
baseline$smoker[baseline$smoker == -999] = NA # Smoker
baseline$phy_activity[baseline$phy_activity == 'Hihg'] = 'High' # Physical activity
baseline$ethnicity[baseline$ethnicity == 4] = NA  # Ethnicity
baseline$bmi[baseline$bmi == 288 | baseline$bmi == 295] = NA # BMI

# Factor type of each categorical variables as new variables
baseline$fsex = factor(baseline$sex, levels = c(1, 2),
    labels = c('Female', 'Male')
)
baseline$fsmoker = factor(baseline$smoker, levels = c(0, 1, 2),
    labels = c('Never smoked', 'Ex smoker', 'Current smoker')
)
baseline$fphy_activity = factor(baseline$phy_activity,
    labels = c('Low', 'Moderate', 'High', 'Very_high')
)
baseline$fdiabetes = factor(baseline$diabetes, levels = c(0, 1),
    labels = c('No', 'Yes')
)
baseline$fethnicity = factor(baseline$ethnicity, levels = c(1, 2, 3),
    labels = c('Group1', 'Group2', 'Group3')
)
baseline$finhaler = factor(baseline$inhaler, levels = c(0, 1),
    labels = c('Not receiving inhaler', 'Receiving inhaler')
)
```

## Visits data

```{r clean-visits}
str(visits)
visits[duplicated(visits), ] # No full duplicates
visits[duplicated(visits[, c('ID', 'visit')]),
    c('ID', 'visit')] # No duplicates by ID and visit
```

| 6 | baseline, bmi | Irregular extreme values | `summary(baseline$bmi)` shows the max value of 295 and ordering the data based on bmi in a descending order shows another improbable bmi value of 288 | Uncertain value | Update values to `NA` | The likeliest value is 29.5 and 28.8 but no way to confirm | 2 rows |


# Missing data

```{r missing, include = FALSE}
# Baseline
colSums(is.na(baseline))

# Smoker
baseline[is.na(baseline$smoker), -1] # No clear pattern

# Physical activity
baseline[is.na(baseline$phy_activity), -1] # No clear pattern

# Diabetes
baseline[is.na(baseline$diabetes), -1] # No clear pattern

# Ethnicity
baseline[is.na(baseline$ethnicity), -1] # No clear pattern

# Visits
colSums(is.na(visits))
kable(table(visits[is.na(visits$walk6min), 'visit']), col.names = c('Visit', 'Total NA'), align = 'l')

invalid_participants = visits[which(visits$visit == 0 & is.na(visits$walk6min)), 'ID']
invalid_participants
nrow(visits[!visits$ID %in% invalid_participants,])
```

Some missing follow-up data is expected and could possibly be because of lost to follow-up. However, missing baseline measure should not happen. Moving on with the analysis, participants with missing baseline will be excluded as they are possibly invalid participants. For the participants with missing follow-up data they will still be analysed but only including the valid data (not NA).

# Data linkage

Since baseline data has 500 rows of data and visits had 3466 rows of data post data cleaning, after merging there should be 3466 rows of data assuming both datasets contains the same unique participant IDs.

*Link the two datasets on the participant identifier. Before linking, work out how many rows you expect, and afterwards check that you have them. Check for identifiers that appear in one dataset but not the other, say which type of merge you used and why, and describe the linked dataset.*

```{r linkage}
linked_data = merge(baseline, visits, by = 'ID',
    all.x = FALSE, all.y = FALSE
)
str(linked_data)
```

The total dataset after merging is 3466 as expected before the join. The inner join is used here because only valid data is needed for analysis, where valid data is participants (ID) that exist in both the baseline and visits dataset. The merged dataset now contains the participant information, characteristics such as pre-existing conditions or exposures, and as well as their baseline measure and all their follow-ups.
